## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `go vet ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/rule/... ./internal/stats/... ./internal/brief/... ./internal/forge/... ./internal/session/... ./internal/sched/... ./internal/config/... ./internal/cli/... ./internal/hub/... ./internal/publish/... ./internal/daemon/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `01` — adds the key `[brief].at`, two routes, two commands, store migrations, hub client calls and shutdown steps to the daemon, and uses its event log, its fake hub and its end-to-end helper
- `02` — reads each workspace's state and daily limit from `workspace.Service`, and registers a function with `OnRemoved`
- `03` — acts on the stored `record` member of an answer, declares the decision kind `rule` and its handlers, writes to the brief thread and the items' threads, reads items, entries and decisions, registers an `OnChange` hook and calls `Notify` with the event `brief`
- `04` — runs the rule's planner session through `Scheduler.RunSession`, extends `session.Spec` for a session with no item, and reads the session records, the pause flags and `Scheduler.Waiting`
- `05` — reads an item's change with `change.Service.Get` for the forge comment, and creates a rule's fork and change with the hub client's `CreateFork`, `OpenChange` and `AbandonChange`
- `06` — reports the three checks of an approved rule with the hub client's `ReportCheck`, reads a fork with `Tree` and `File` and a change with `Change`, and lists in the brief the files `(*impl.Service).OutsidePlan` returns
- `07` — lands a rule's change with `land.Service.LandChange`, and reads the commit an item's change landed as with `land.Service.Landing`
- `08` — runs the sync before a rule's landing with `publish.Service.Sync`, checks the landed commit with `health.Service.VerifyTip`, adds `PushTip` to `internal/publish`, and repeats its `published` entry in the brief
- `09` — counts the items taken over from its thread entry, and shows its marker `taken over` as what an item waits for

- 2.1 Add the answer, landing, revise and discard behaviours to the new internal/rule/land_test.go and confirm they fail; extend internal/hubtest, where an earlier package left it out, with the check route (the reports kept per change, version and name), the land route with a scriptable answer per change (landed with a commit, 409 land_conflict, 409 policy_blocked, 409 version_mismatch, 503 land_failed) and a request log that keeps the order of the requests
- 2.2 Add to package 08's internal/publish a function that is new, Service.PushTip(ctx, slug) (bool, error), with its behaviours in internal/publish/push_test.go: package 08 pushes only for an item (PublishStep) or for an answered `origin` decision (Retry), and a landed rule has neither. It refuses without a request while the workspace is not green, health.TipPending(slug) is true or the hub is unavailable, sends one Push of the default branch otherwise, and opens no decision, sets no state, writes no entry and starts no tries. Then give the rule service four functions at its creation, so that its tests can replace them, and have daemon.Run pass the real ones: publish.Service.Sync (the sync before a landing with what its result starts), land.Service.LandChange, health.Service.VerifyTip and publish.Service.PushTip
- 2.3 Register with OnAnswer the handlers of (`rule`, `approve`), (`rule`, `revise`) and (`rule`, `discard`): each finds the rule by the decision it was opened for, changes the rule's state only when the rule is `proposed` for that decision (to `approved`, to `writing` with the comment stored, to `discarded` after the abandon), and returns nil when the rule is already past that point, so that a second call does nothing
- 2.4 In Pass, for a rule in `approved`: go on only when workspace.Service.Get reports `green`, the scheduler's pause flag of the workspace is not set (add an accessor for the workspace's flag to internal/sched where there is none) and hub.Available(worker) is true; then call the sync function (publish.Service.Sync) and go on only when it returned no error
- 2.5 Read the change with GET …/changes/{number}: when its state is `landed`, take landed.sha and go to the landed step; when it is `abandoned`, set the rule `failed`; otherwise report the three checks on its current version through the hub client's ReportCheck of package 06 (its (*impl.Service).ReportCheck is bound to an item) with the status passed and the summary `rule approved by the owner`, remembering the version they were reported for so that a second Pass does not report them again, and call LandChange with the workspace, the change and that version; LandChange checks no condition and reports no check itself
- 2.6 On an Outcome of the kind `landed`: store LandedSHA and the state `landed` and append `rule_landed`; then, once per rule (the stored hand-over mark is set before the calls), call VerifyTip with the workspace and the commit and, when it returns nil, PushTip; when that returns true, set `published`, append `rule_published` and call RemoveScope; when VerifyTip returns an error (it has set the workspace red and opened `main_red` itself) or PushTip returns false, leave the rule `landed` and do nothing more: the commit reaches origin with the next push package 08 sends for the branch
- 2.7 On an Outcome of any other kind: abandon the change with the hub client's AbandonChange (409 change_closed counts as done), set `failed`, append `rule_failed` with `rule for decision <id> not landed: <kind>`, and `: <reason>` where the outcome has one, and the unread mark, and call RemoveScope
- 2.8 For a rule set to `writing` by `revise`: ask for the session on the change's branch with the inputs `rule` and `comment`; judge the branch as task 1 does; on success read the change's new version from the hub, set `proposed` and open a new `rule` decision; a failure stays on the same branch and the second in a row ends the rule as task 1 says, abandoning the change
- 2.9 For `discard`: abandon the change with the hub client's AbandonChange of package 05, taking 409 change_closed as done, append `rule_discarded` and call RemoveScope
- 2.10 Add the flow of a recorded answer that reaches origin to internal/daemon/e2e_test.go, with the fake `claude` helper of package 04 writing the ADR and with the real functions of packages 07 and 08, and describe the way of a rule from the answer to origin, what it takes from packages 05 to 08 and the new publish.Service.PushTip in docs/architecture.md

### 3. Count the outcome numbers and print them with nightshift stats (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Add the number behaviours to the new internal/stats/stats_test.go and internal/stats/routes_test.go and the command's to internal/cli/cli_test.go, and confirm they fail; write the seed helper of internal/stats: it creates items through the item service and walks them through allowed transitions with the injected clock, writes session records through a function of internal/session (add one that stores a finished session's record for tests where package 04 has none), appends entries with the inbox's Append, and opens and answers decisions of a test kind
- 3.2 Add to internal/session, where package 04 has none, a read of the session records by item and by workspace with each record's role, status, tokens, start and end time; the tokens are the count package 04 keeps (input, cache-creation and output tokens)
- 3.3 Add internal/stats.Compute(ctx, slug, days), with the clock injected: the window is the days times 24 hours before now; the done items are the workspace's items in `done` whose state_since lies in the window, the abandoned ones likewise
- 3.4 Compute first_pass and sessions_per_item from the session records of each done item (package 06 asks a rework session with the step name `implement`, as a first one, so the records' order is what tells them apart): an item is a first pass when no implementer record starts after the end of its first implementer record with the status completed, and also when it has no completed implementer record; the share is rounded to the nearest whole percent
- 3.5 Compute reverted and taken_over by reading the entries of the threads of the workspace's items: an item counts once when an entry of kind `state` whose text begins `verifying -> awaiting_approval`, or an entry of kind `taken_over` (package 09 writes one for each take-over), has its time in the window
- 3.6 Compute decisions_per_done_item from the answered decisions of the done items' threads, decision_wait_seconds from the decisions of every thread of the workspace (the items' and the workspace's own) whose answer's time lies in the window, creation_to_done_seconds from created_at and state_since, and tokens_per_done_item from the summed tokens of each done item's records; one median function (the mean of the two middle values for an even count), and null for a number whose base is empty
- 3.7 Serve GET /api/v1/stats through the API server's Handle: `days` absent is 30, anything but a decimal integer from 1 to 365 is 400 invalid_request, an unregistered `workspace` is 404 not_found, no `workspace` is every registered workspace in order of slug
- 3.8 Register the command `nightshift stats [<slug>] [--days <N>]` through the client's Register: check `--days` and the argument count before any request (exit code 2 with the usage), print the block of each workspace, and the API's JSON with --json; put the formatting of a duration, of a null and of a number with at most one decimal into exported functions of internal/stats, for the brief to use
- 3.9 Describe GET /api/v1/stats with every member and how it is counted in docs/api.md, and `nightshift stats` in docs/cli.md

### 5. Write back to the issue an item was imported from (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-5

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the write-back behaviours to the new internal/forge/forge_test.go and confirm they fail; extend internal/hubtest with POST …/issues/{number}/comments (the comments kept per issue; a request whose Idempotency-Key was answered successfully before answers 200 and adds nothing), POST …/issues/{number}/close (the issue's state, a body with a comment adds the comment), a scriptable error per route and call, and accessors for an issue's comments and state
- 5.2 Add internal/forge with its store migration: one row per write with the item, the workspace, the issue's number, what it is for (approved, done, reverted, abandoned), its body, whether the comment was taken, whether a close follows and was taken, the time of its first try, the time of its next try, and whether it was given up
- 5.3 Register a hook with item.OnChange that, for an item whose source type is `issue` and nothing else, records a write and returns without any request: `approved` for a move to `ready` from `planning` or `awaiting_approval`, `done` for a move to `done`, `reverted` for a move from `verifying` to `awaiting_approval`, `abandoned` for a move to `abandoned`; a second hook call for the same transition records nothing
- 5.4 Build each body when its write is first tried: the change's number from Change of the record package 05's change.Service.Get returns, the hub's endpoint from the configuration, and for `done` the LandedSHA of package 07's land.Service.Landing; both lookups are given to the writer as functions, and one that fails or answers no change or no commit is a failed try of the write
- 5.5 Add the writer's Pass, run at an interval that is a parameter and stopped with the daemon: for each item with writes not yet taken or given up, take the oldest alone; when its next try is due, send the comment with the worker credential and the header Idempotency-Key `nightshift-forge-<write id>`, and for `done`, after the comment was taken, the close with no body; add to the hub client of internal/hub the two calls
- 5.6 On a failed call, and when hub.Available(worker) is false, set the first try's time where it is not set and the next try to 10 minutes later, both from the injected clock and both intervals parameters with the defaults 10 minutes and 24 hours; when the failed try is 24 hours or more after the first, mark the write given up and append the `forge_failed` entry with `could not write to issue #<N>: <error_type>: <message>`, or the transport error's text, without the unread mark
- 5.7 At Start, for every item whose source type is `issue` and whose state is `done` or `abandoned`, record the write of that state where the item has none for it
- 5.8 Register a function with workspace.Service.OnRemoved that removes the writes of the removed workspace's items, since their threads are gone
- 5.9 Create the writer in daemon.Run after the item service and the hub client, and add the flow of an imported issue across a forge outage to internal/daemon/e2e_test.go
- 5.10 Describe internal/forge, the four writes, the retry and what it reads from packages 05 and 07 in docs/architecture.md; say in docs/configuration.md that the worker token's `forge:write` is what the write-back uses and that the workspace needs a forge credential on the hub; run `make doc`
